Store

Concept 7 · Direction: Apple-inspired: shop shelves

Borrows the logic of a modern online store page, not its look. The page opens with one sentence (‘Shop. Motocaddy trolleys and custom‑fitted clubs, with free fitting in Ringwood.’) and two human routes (talk to a fitter, visit). A row of picture tiles makes every category one tap away, with fitting and membership sitting alongside products as equals. Each shelf then answers one question with a bold lead and a lighter follow-on: the latest Motocaddy range; help choosing (fitting, trolley finder, call, visit); clubs built your way; membership; buying guides. Shelves scroll sideways, so the page stays short even with all eight trolleys on it.

Structural changes from the brief’s section order

The hero shrinks to a one-line intro; the category row replaces the main nav’s job on the homepage. Fitting is presented twice: as a category tile and as the first card of the ‘Help choosing’ shelf. The trust row and reviews reduce to fine print at the foot (until real reviews are connected).

Typefaces

EverythingInter (variable)Google Fonts, SIL OFL; stands in for SF Pro. Shelf titles pair a bold lead with a lighter grey follow-on.

Key components (rendered from the concept’s own CSS)

Shelf title. Bold lead plus lighter continuation, the only heading style on the page.

The latest. The 2026 Motocaddy range.

Product card. Large rounded white card: stock flag in green, name, one spec line, price, product image at the foot.

  • In stock Motocaddy M5 GPS DHC GPS · Downhill control · 18 or 36 holes From £969

Category row. Picture tiles for every department; services (fitting, membership, trade-in, sale) use line icons on a tint.

Imagery and photography

Clean product cut-outs at the foot of white cards; picture tiles in the category row. Very little lifestyle photography is needed; the guides shelf can carry the few documentary shots (fitting, the shop floor).

Headline copy

H1: “Shop. Motocaddy trolleys and custom‑fitted clubs, with free fitting in Ringwood.”

Shelves: “The latest.” · “Help choosing.” · “Clubs, your way.” · “Membership.” · “Read before you buy.”

Motion

Shelves scroll with momentum and snap to cards; cards lift slightly on hover. Nothing on load.

Trade-offs

Does wellMost shoppable of the Apple-inspired three: every category and all eight trolleys within two screens; services sit alongside products, so fitting and membership feel like things you can ‘get’; very low photography needs.
Weaker onRounded white cards in rows are the closest of all seven concepts to the generic look you wanted to leave behind; horizontal shelves hide items off-screen on desktop; relies on very good card copy to feel premium.
Build effortLow–medium: one card component in a few variants plus a scroll-snap shelf; category row from a menu.
Photography neededLow: cut-outs already available; a few documentary shots for the guides.
Suits bestReturning customers and members who know what they want; mobile shoppers browsing by category.

EG monogram: ‘EG’ in a small rounded ink square in the header (suggestion only; the mark itself isn’t being redesigned here).
